en: you've ever planned something big and then done absolutely nothing about it,
zh: 如果你曾经计划过一件大事，结果却完全没有行动，

en: it is not because you're lazy.
zh: 那并不是因为你懒。

en: There's literally a neurological cycle happening in your brain.
zh: 你的大脑里真的正在发生一个神经循环。

en: that prevents you from pursuing your dreams.
zh: 它会阻止你去追求自己的梦想。

en: and in this video I'll explain how it works and how to fix it.
zh: 在这个视频里，我会解释它是怎么运作的，以及该如何修复它。

en: My name is Olga, I study cognitive science and computation at the University of Pennsylvania.
zh: 我叫 Olga，我在宾夕法尼亚大学学习认知科学与计算。

en: and after the last four years of studying how the human mind works.
zh: 在过去四年里，我一直在研究人类心智是如何运作的。

en: I think this is probably most fascinating and most useful thing I learned about.
zh: 我觉得这大概是我学到的最有趣、也最有用的东西。

en: So procrastination researcher Tim Pychyl has spent decades studying why people don't do the things.
zh: 所以，拖延症研究者 Tim Pychyl 花了几十年研究为什么人们不去做那些事情。

en: that they promised themselves to do.
zh: 也就是他们曾经承诺自己要做的事情。

en: and he found that procrastination is not a time management problem.
zh: 他发现，拖延并不是一个时间管理问题。

en: procrastination is an emotion regulation problem.
zh: 拖延是一个情绪调节问题。

en: and here's what it means.
zh: 这句话的意思是这样的。

en: When you have something important to do.
zh: 当你有一件重要的事情要做时。

en: like starting a creative project or submitting an application or doing a workout or an assignment.
zh: 比如开始一个创意项目、提交一份申请、锻炼，或者完成一项作业。

en: and you think about actually doing it, that's when your brain generates a negative emotion.
zh: 当你想到自己真的要去做它时，你的大脑就会产生一种负面情绪。

en: It can be self-doubt, overwhelm, anxiety.
zh: 它可能是自我怀疑、压力过大，或者焦虑。

en: you might have fear that the result is not going to be good enough.
zh: 你可能会害怕结果不够好。

en: and your brain does not like negative emotions, so it escapes.
zh: 而你的大脑不喜欢负面情绪，所以它会逃避。

en: You start cleaning your room, you reorganize your desk.
zh: 你开始打扫房间，重新整理书桌。

en: you pick up your phone, you start scrolling.
zh: 你拿起手机，开始刷起来。

en: and suddenly that negative feeling of dread goes away.
zh: 突然之间，那种恐惧和压力的负面感觉就消失了。

en: and you feel relief.
zh: 然后你感到松了一口气。

en: and here's an interesting part.
zh: 有意思的地方来了。

en: That relief in itself is a reward.
zh: 这种松一口气的感觉本身就是一种奖励。

en: and in psychology behaviors that get rewarded get repeated.
zh: 在心理学中，获得奖励的行为会被重复。

en: so your brain learns if I avoid a difficult task.
zh: 所以你的大脑会学到：如果我逃避一项困难的任务。

en: that's when I'm going to get that short-term feeling of relief.
zh: 我就会获得那种短暂的轻松感。

en: which is something positive.
zh: 而这是一种积极的感受。

en: and it starts doing it automatically every time you're faced with something difficult.
zh: 于是每当你面对困难的事情时，它就会开始自动这样做。

en: and your brain creates something called an avoidance loop.
zh: 你的大脑会制造出一种叫作逃避循环的东西。

en: where you're faced with a difficult task, it triggers a negative emotion.
zh: 也就是当你面对一项困难任务时，它会触发负面情绪。

en: then you don't do that task.
zh: 然后你不去做那项任务。

en: so you feel relief.
zh: 于是你感到轻松。

en: and next time you're faced with something difficult you again default to avoidance.
zh: 下次你再面对困难的事情时，你又会默认选择逃避。

en: because that's what triggers relief.
zh: 因为逃避会触发轻松感。

en: and here's what's happening in your brain.
zh: 而这就是你大脑里正在发生的事情。

en: Every time you're faced with a hard task.
zh: 每当你面对一项困难任务时。

en: there are two systems that are competing for control.
zh: 有两个系统在争夺控制权。

en: and the first is your amygdala which is your brain's alarm system.
zh: 第一个是你的杏仁核，也就是大脑的警报系统。

en: It is essentially responsible for detecting threats in the environment.
zh: 它本质上负责探测环境中的威胁。

en: and if a task is seeming overwhelming or scary to you.
zh: 如果一项任务让你觉得压力很大，或者很可怕。

en: it essentially treats that task as a threat.
zh: 它基本上就会把这项任务当成一种威胁。

en: so it tells you don't do this run.
zh: 于是它会告诉你：不要做这个，快跑。

en: this is dangerous you have to avoid this.
zh: 这很危险，你必须避开它。

en: and the second is the part of your brain.
zh: 第二个是你大脑中的另一个部分。

en: that actually makes you act.
zh: 它是真正让你采取行动的部分。

en: and neuroscientists call it the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex.
zh: 神经科学家把它叫作背侧前扣带皮层。

en: essentially it takes the fear signal from the amygdala.
zh: 本质上，它会接收来自杏仁核的恐惧信号。

en: if needed it shuts it down.
zh: 如果有必要，它会把这个信号压下去。

en: and then it actually pushes you to do the things that you're supposed to be doing.
zh: 然后它会真正推动你去做那些你本该做的事情。

en: and when you procrastinate your amygdala is winning.
zh: 而当你拖延时，是你的杏仁核赢了。

en: which is called an amygdala hijack.
zh: 这叫作杏仁核劫持。

en: where essentially your emotional brain overrides your irrational brain.
zh: 本质上就是你的情绪大脑压过了你的非理性大脑。

en: and you flee from the task.
zh: 然后你从任务面前逃走了。

en: and here's why it gets worse if you don't address it.
zh: 这也是为什么如果你不处理它，情况会变得更糟。

en: every time you're going through the avoidance loop.
zh: 每当你经历一次逃避循环时。

en: you feel dread towards the task.
zh: 你会对任务感到恐惧。

en: you avoid it you feel relief.
zh: 你逃避它，然后你感到轻松。

en: every time you go through this avoidance loop.
zh: 每当你经历一次这样的逃避循环。

en: you are physically strengthening the neural pathway for procrastination.
zh: 你都在从生理上强化拖延的神经通路。

en: because as we all know what you repeat you become.
zh: 因为我们都知道，你反复做什么，你就会变成什么样。

en: so the procrastination circuit gets faster.
zh: 所以拖延回路会变得更快。

en: it becomes more of a default behavior for you.
zh: 它会越来越成为你的默认行为。

en: and your discipline circuit weakens.
zh: 而你的自律回路会变弱。

en: like a muscle that you stopped using.
zh: 就像一块你停止使用的肌肉。

en: so if your brain is training itself to avoid and procrastinate.
zh: 所以，如果你的大脑正在训练自己去逃避和拖延。

en: could you theoretically train it to do the complete opposite.
zh: 那理论上你能不能训练它做完全相反的事情呢？

en: well Tim Pychyl spent 20 years of his career trying to answer that question.
zh: Tim Pychyl 花了职业生涯中的 20 年试图回答这个问题。

en: well the answer is embarrassingly simple.
zh: 答案简单到有点让人尴尬。

en: and the answer is you have to just start.
zh: 答案就是：你必须直接开始。

en: just start that's it.
zh: 直接开始，就这样。

en: no need to finish it.
zh: 不需要把它完成。

en: no need to perform well.
zh: 不需要表现得很好。

en: we just have to start the task for five to ten minutes.
zh: 我们只需要开始做这项任务五到十分钟。

en: and not think about the outcome.
zh: 不要去想结果。

en: essentially you have to learn to interrupt the avoidance loop.
zh: 本质上，你必须学会打断逃避循环。

en: and here's how you do it.
zh: 方法是这样的。

en: step number one is to catch it and name it.
zh: 第一步，是捕捉到它，并说出它的名字。

en: and when you notice yourself procrastinating.
zh: 当你注意到自己正在拖延时。

en: and you notice yourself avoiding something.
zh: 当你注意到自己正在逃避某件事时。

en: think about the emotion you're experiencing.
zh: 想一想你正在经历的情绪是什么。

en: are you feeling overwhelmed.
zh: 你是不是感到不堪重负？

en: are you feeling anxious.
zh: 你是不是感到焦虑？

en: are you afraid that your result is not going to be good enough.
zh: 你是不是害怕自己的结果不够好？

en: just naming that emotion is enough for you.
zh: 仅仅说出这种情绪，对你来说就已经足够了。

en: to switch from your emotional mind back into your rational mind.
zh: 它能让你从情绪脑切换回理性脑。

en: and second step is to make your task stupidly small.
zh: 第二步，是把你的任务缩小到蠢到不能再小。

en: essentially think about what is the tiniest possible action.
zh: 本质上，你要想一想，最小的可能行动是什么。

en: you can set for yourself as the goal.
zh: 你可以把它设定为自己的目标。

en: just to make at least a little bit of progress.
zh: 只是为了至少取得一点点进展。

en: for example don't think that you have to write a whole essay tonight.
zh: 比如，不要想着你今晚必须写完整篇论文。

en: think oh my task is to open the document in google doc.
zh: 你可以想：哦，我的任务是在 Google 文档里打开这个文件。

en: and write for just 10 minutes.
zh: 然后只写 10 分钟。

en: and don't think oh i have to do this hour-long workout.
zh: 也不要想着：哦，我必须完成这一小时的锻炼。

en: i'm really dreading it.
zh: 我真的很抗拒它。

en: think of your task as just putting on your shoes.
zh: 把你的任务想成只是穿上鞋。

en: and going outside.
zh: 然后走到外面去。

en: and the reason why simply starting something for 10 minutes is so powerful.
zh: 仅仅开始做一件事 10 分钟之所以如此强大。

en: is because the actual process of completing a task.
zh: 是因为真正完成一项任务的过程。

en: it's almost always much easier.
zh: 几乎总是要容易得多。

en: than the extreme dread you feel before doing it.
zh: 比起你在做它之前感受到的那种极端恐惧。

en: and Pychyl showed this beautifully in this study.
zh: Pychyl 在这项研究中非常漂亮地展示了这一点。

en: where he gave 45 students pagers.
zh: 他给了 45 名学生传呼机。

en: and that was before smartphones existed.
zh: 那是在智能手机出现之前。

en: so he gave them pagers.
zh: 所以他给了他们传呼机。

en: he would page them eight times a day for five days.
zh: 在他们某门课的学术截止日期到来前的五天里。

en: leading up to their academic deadline on some in some class.
zh: 他每天会呼叫他们八次。

en: and when the pager went off the student was supposed to report.
zh: 当传呼机响起时，学生需要报告。

en: how they were feeling.
zh: 他们当时感觉如何。

en: what they were doing.
zh: 他们当时在做什么。

en: how they were feeling about the academic assignment that they had to do.
zh: 以及他们对自己必须完成的那项学术作业感觉如何。

en: the data showed that the students consistently procrastinated on the tasks.
zh: 数据显示，学生们会持续拖延那些任务。

en: that they found difficult or unpleasant or stressful.
zh: 也就是那些他们觉得困难、不愉快，或者有压力的任务。

en: and they consistently replaced them with activities.
zh: 他们会持续用其他活动来替代这些任务。

en: that were more interesting and more exciting.
zh: 那些活动更有趣，也更让人兴奋。

en: and of course we all would do that right.
zh: 当然，我们都会这么做，对吧。

en: but here's what Pychyl found most interesting.
zh: 但 Pychyl 觉得最有意思的是这一点。

en: when students procrastinated early in the week.
zh: 当学生在一周早些时候拖延时。

en: they would constantly justify it.
zh: 他们会不断为自己找理由。

en: they would constantly say that oh i work better under pressure.
zh: 他们会不停地说，哦，我在压力下工作得更好。

en: and work better close to the deadline.
zh: 越接近截止日期，我工作得越好。

en: i will feel like it tomorrow.
zh: 我明天就会有心情做了。

en: and they would say things like these.
zh: 他们会说这些类似的话。

en: to explain why they're not doing the task.
zh: 来解释为什么他们没有做那项任务。

en: they're supposed to be doing.
zh: 也就是他们本该做的任务。

en: but when the deadline actually forced them to start.
zh: 但当截止日期真的迫使他们开始时。

en: not one of them said that they were glad they waited.
zh: 没有一个人说自己很庆幸当初等到了现在。

en: they were all saying that they wish they had more time.
zh: 他们都说希望自己有更多时间。

en: they wish they started earlier.
zh: 他们希望自己早点开始。

en: and that the task wasn't actually as bad as they thought.
zh: 而且那项任务其实并没有他们想的那么糟。

en: so you're not actually avoiding the task.
zh: 所以你真正逃避的并不是任务本身。

en: you're avoiding the way that you think the task is going to make you feel.
zh: 你逃避的是你以为这项任务会带给你的感受。

en: and your brain is wrong about it almost all of the time.
zh: 而你的大脑几乎每次在这件事上都是错的。

en: and now you might be thinking.
zh: 现在你可能会想。

en: well i don't just sit on the couch doing nothing.
zh: 可是我并不是坐在沙发上什么都不做。

en: i'm actually busy all the time.
zh: 我其实一直都很忙。

en: so why can i not finally start this project that i've been putting off for months.
zh: 那为什么我还是没法真正开始这个已经拖了好几个月的项目呢？

en: well there's an answer to that.
zh: 这个问题是有答案的。

en: your brain does not just let you sit there doing nothing.
zh: 你的大脑不会只是让你坐在那里什么都不做。

en: because that triggers guilt.
zh: 因为那会触发内疚感。

en: and guilt is another negative emotion.
zh: 而内疚感也是另一种负面情绪。

en: that and they do as trying to escape.
zh: 它们也会试图逃离这种情绪。

en: so it disguises that avoidance as productivity.
zh: 所以它会把逃避伪装成生产力。

en: and there's actually two specific disguises.
zh: 实际上有两种具体的伪装方式。

en: that i want to discuss with you.
zh: 我想和你们讨论一下。

en: and the first disguise is perfectionism.
zh: 第一种伪装是完美主义。

en: and research has consistently shown that people who score higher on perfectionism are bigger procrastinators.
zh: 研究一直显示，完美主义得分越高的人，拖延越严重。

en: because perfectionism essentially makes you afraid.
zh: 因为完美主义本质上会让你害怕。

en: that your result is not going to be good enough.
zh: 害怕你的结果不够好。

en: which makes you not even start in the first place.
zh: 这会让你一开始就根本不行动。

en: and researchers found that more perfectionist professors actually publish less papers.
zh: 研究人员发现，更完美主义的教授实际上发表的论文更少。

en: than their last perfectionist colleagues.
zh: 比起那些不那么完美主义的同事。

en: even if control for how hardworking they are.
zh: 即使控制了他们的勤奋程度也是如此。

en: essentially perfectionism makes you never start.
zh: 本质上，完美主义会让你永远无法开始。

en: so you never fall short.
zh: 这样你就永远不会达不到标准。

en: and disguise number two is productive procrastination.
zh: 第二种伪装是生产性拖延。

en: and this one gets everyone.
zh: 这一种每个人都会中招。

en: it's the sneakiest one.
zh: 它是最隐蔽的一种。

en: because you're not actually sitting on the couch.
zh: 因为你并不是真的坐在沙发上。

en: you are doing something.
zh: 你是在做一些事情。

en: you're researching. you're reorganizing your desk.
zh: 你在做调研。你在重新整理书桌。

en: you're planning something.
zh: 你在计划某件事。

en: you're watching videos on youtube about how to be more productive.
zh: 你在 YouTube 上看关于如何提高效率的视频。

en: instead of actually doing the thing.
zh: 而不是实际去做那件真正该做的事。

en: maybe you're watching this video right now.
zh: 也许你现在就在看这个视频。

en: instead of working on your assignment or working on your new project.
zh: 而不是写你的作业，或者推进你的新项目。

en: i don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

en: and Pychyl's research calls this short-term mood repair.
zh: Pychyl 的研究把这称为短期情绪修复。

en: when a real task triggers anxiety or overwhelm or some negative emotion.
zh: 当一项真正的任务触发焦虑、压力过大，或者某种负面情绪时。

en: your brain essentially decides to swap it.
zh: 你的大脑本质上会决定把它替换掉。

en: for a safer and less risky task.
zh: 换成一项更安全、风险更低的任务。

en: that is still going to give you some sense of accomplishment.
zh: 这项任务仍然会给你一些成就感。

en: when you finish it.
zh: 当你完成它的时候。

en: but it's going to be without any risk of failure or judgment.
zh: 但它不会带来任何失败或被评判的风险。

en: because that task is going to be less high stakes.
zh: 因为那项任务的利害关系更低。

en: like instead of writing an essay.
zh: 比如，你没有去写论文。

en: you spent an hour color coding your notes.
zh: 而是花了一个小时给笔记做颜色分类。

en: or instead of applying to jobs.
zh: 或者你没有去投工作。

en: you spent hours perfecting your resume for the fifth time.
zh: 而是花了好几个小时第五次打磨你的简历。

en: and instead of starting a business.
zh: 你没有去开始创业。

en: that you've jumped up starting for years.
zh: 那个你已经幻想要开始很多年的事情。

en: you read 10 books on how to start a business.
zh: 而是读了 10 本关于如何创业的书。

en: so you feel like you're making some progress.
zh: 所以你感觉自己好像在取得一些进展。

en: but the actual scary task that you actually have to do hasn't moved an inch.
zh: 但那个你真正必须去做、真正可怕的任务却一点都没有推进。

en: and again remember you're not actually avoiding the task.
zh: 再次记住，你真正逃避的并不是任务本身。

en: you're avoiding how you think the task is going to make you feel.
zh: 你逃避的是你以为这项任务会带给你的感受。

en: but when you actually start doing it.
zh: 但当你真的开始做它时。

en: you realize that the dread of starting is much worse.
zh: 你会意识到，开始之前的那种恐惧要糟糕得多。

en: than doing most of the time.
zh: 比真正去做这件事本身糟糕得多，大多数时候都是这样。

en: so now you know what the avoidance loop looks like.
zh: 所以现在你知道逃避循环是什么样子了。

en: how your brain disguises it.
zh: 也知道你的大脑是如何伪装它的。

en: and how to break it.
zh: 以及如何打破它。

en: so subscribe if this helped.
zh: 如果这个视频帮到了你，记得订阅。

en: and please let me know in the comments what other topics or videos.
zh: 也请在评论区告诉我，你们还想在我的 YouTube 频道上看到哪些主题、视频。

en: or ideas you would like to see in my youtube channel.
zh: 或者哪些想法。

en: and i'm currently building out my youtube channel.
zh: 我现在正在建设我的 YouTube 频道。

en: so any sort of support or likes or comments would be greatly appreciated.
zh: 所以任何形式的支持、点赞或评论，我都会非常感激。

en: and i'll see you in the next one.
zh: 我们下期视频见。
